Resolves #19138

Adds four native-browser cases for `Neo.layout.Fit`: the child fills a rendered 300 × 200 container, keeps its own class, respects `ignoreLayout`, and loses the Fit classes when the container switches to VBox. The existing empty viewport and App Worker creation/configuration APIs own setup and teardown.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium component tier, native geometry and class observations) → L3 required. No residual acceptance obligations.

Micro-review eligible: test-only — one spec pins existing layout behavior without changing production source.

## Deltas from ticket

The fixture uses the public `width` / `height` configs instead of the illustrative CSS-only size, so its parent VBox recognizes the fixed height. The switch control reads computed column direction rather than guessing a VBox class. [Retained fixture calibration](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19138#issuecomment-6688145216).

All coverage runs in CI.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical (test-only). One new component spec pins existing `Neo.layout.Fit` behavior, and production source is unchanged.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** I read the spec at head `1d5510f9a1` against the four rows of #19138. Each row has its own `test(...)`. CI ran all four in `components (2/3)` of run 42244306525, cases 113–116. I checked whether each pass witnesses something:
- Row 1 measures the rendered boxes. Without the fit CSS, a `component` with text would be content-height, not 200 px.
- Row 3 checks the ignored child only after the managed child carries `neo-layout-fit-item`, so the layout has run when the absence is read.
- Row 4 waits for VBox's `flex-direction: column` before reading the removed classes.

I found no fixed sleep, no reading back of a class the test itself wrote, and no edit outside the new file. The `width`/`height` configs in place of the ticket's `style` are a justified delta. The parent VBox needs the logical size, and the calibration comment on #19138 records why.
